stem: Which of the following is three million, forty thousand and six written in numerals?
working: Three million: the 3 goes in the millions place.
Forty thousand: the thousands group is 040 (a 4 in the ten thousands place).
Six: the ones group is 006.
So the number is 3 040 006.

distractors.2: This is three million, four hundred thousand and six. The 4 belongs in the ten thousands place.
distractors.3: This number ends in sixty, not six. The 6 goes in the ones place.
distractors.4: This is three hundred and forty thousand and six. Three million needs seven digits.

hints: Write the number in three groups: millions, thousands, then ones.
Every group after the millions has exactly three digits. Fill the empty places with zeros.

stem: A number rounded to the nearest thousand is 58 000. Which of the following could be the number?

58 501 and 58 500: the hundreds digit is 5, so they round up to 59 000.
57 850: the hundreds digit is 8, so it rounds up to 58 000 ✓

distractors.1: 57 499 is just below 57 500, so it rounds down to 57 000.
distractors.2: The hundreds digit is 5, so 58 501 rounds up to 59 000.
distractors.4: 58 500 is exactly halfway. A 5 in the hundreds place rounds up, to 59 000.

hints: Look at the hundreds digit: 5 or more rounds up, 4 or less rounds down.

stem: Find the value of 90 − 36 ÷ (4 + 2) × 3.
working: Brackets first: 4 + 2 = 6.
Then divide and multiply from left to right: 36 ÷ 6 = 6, then 6 × 3 = 18.
Subtract last: 90 − 18 = 72.

distractors.1: Subtracted first (90 − 36). Division and multiplication come before subtraction.
distractors.2: Multiplied 6 × 3 before dividing. Division and multiplication go from left to right, so 36 ÷ 6 comes first.
distractors.3: Left out the brackets. Work out 4 + 2 first.

hints: Brackets first, then ÷ and × from left to right, then + and −.
After the brackets, the next step is the division.

hints: How many sticks are added each time the figure grows by one square?

stem: 3 pencil cases cost the same as 5 files. Each pencil case costs $4 more than each file. Kumar bought 4 pencil cases and some files. He paid $76 altogether. How many files did he buy?
working: Each pencil case costs 1 file + $4, so 3 pencil cases cost 3 files + $12.
3 pencil cases cost the same as 5 files, so 5 files = 3 files + $12 → 2 files cost $12 → 1 file costs $6.
1 pencil case costs $6 + $4 = $10, so 4 pencil cases cost 4 × $10 = $40.
Money left for files: $76 − $40 = $36. Number of files = $36 ÷ $6 = 6.
hints: Draw 3 pencil cases as 3 files plus the extra money.

stem: Box A had 3 times as many marbles as Box B. After 85 marbles were moved from Box A to Box B, Box B had 2 times as many marbles as Box A. How many marbles were in Box A at first?
working: Marbles are only moved between the boxes, so the TOTAL stays the same.
Before: A = 3 parts, B = 1 part, so the total is 4 parts. After: A = 1 part, B = 2 parts, so the total is 3 parts.
Make the totals the same: use 12 units. Before: A = 9 u, B = 3 u. After: A = 4 u, B = 8 u.
Box A went from 9 u to 4 u, so 5 u = 85 marbles → 1 u = 17.
Box A at first = 9 × 17 = 153 marbles.
hints: Marbles only move from one box to the other. What stays the same?
Before, the total is 4 parts; after, it is 3 parts. Change both into the same number of units, then see how many units Box A lost.

stem: A jar with 30 identical marbles in it has a mass of 1.32 kg. After 12 of the marbles are taken out, the jar and the remaining marbles have a mass of 1.008 kg. Some marbles are then put back into the jar until the jar and the marbles have a mass of 1.19 kg. How many marbles are in the jar now?

After 12 are taken out, 18 marbles are left. Mass added when marbles are put back: 1.19 − 1.008 = 0.182 kg.
Marbles put back: 0.182 ÷ 0.026 = 7. Marbles now: 18 + 7 = 25.
hints: The drop from 1.32 kg to 1.008 kg is the mass of the 12 marbles taken out.

stem:
Three ferries leave a jetty for an island. Each trip normally takes the same amount of time.

- Ferry A: leaves at 08 45, arrives at 10 10
- Ferry B: leaves at 11 20, arrives at 12 45
- Ferry C: leaves at 14 50

On its trip, Ferry C stopped for an extra 35 minutes because of bad weather. At what time did Ferry C arrive at the island? Give your answer in the 24-hour clock.
working: Ferry A: 08 45 → 09 45 is 1 h and 09 45 → 10 10 is 25 min, so one trip takes 1 h 25 min (Ferry B: 11 20 → 12 45 ✓).
Ferry C without the stop: 14 50 + 1 h = 15 50, then + 25 min = 16 15.
With the extra 35 min: 16 15 + 35 min = 16 50.
hints: Use Ferry A or Ferry B to find how long one trip takes.

stem: A machine prints 45 posters every 2 minutes. It starts printing at 9.40 a.m. After printing 900 posters, it stops for a 15-minute break. Then it prints another 720 posters at the same rate. At what time does it finish printing?

hints: Find how many lots of 45 posters there are in 900, and how many minutes that takes.

stem: The figure shows the net of a cuboid. It is made up of 2 squares and 4 identical rectangles. Each rectangle is as wide as a side of the square and 3 times as long as it is wide. The total area of the net is 224 cm². Find the volume of the cuboid.
working: Each rectangle is as wide as a square and 3 times as long, so one rectangle has the same area as 3 squares.
Total: 2 squares + 4 × 3 squares = 14 squares = 224 cm², so 1 square = 224 ÷ 14 = 16 cm².
The side of a square is 4 cm (4 × 4 = 16), so each rectangle is 4 cm by 12 cm.
The cuboid is 4 cm by 4 cm by 12 cm. Volume = 4 × 4 × 12 = 192 cm³.
hints: How many of the squares would cover one rectangle exactly?
